tasks.entryName: Montel's theorem (locally bounded holomorphic families are normal)
tasks.entryDescription: Arzelà–Ascoli plus Cauchy estimates; diagonal compactness on compact subsets; equicontinuity and holomorphic limit arguments.
tasks.currentSketch: Local boundedness gives uniform equicontinuity on compact sets (Cauchy estimates, proved in the previous lecture). On each compact K, Arzelà–Ascoli then gives a subsequence converging uniformly on K. Taking an exhaustion K₁⊂K₂⊂… by compact sets, successively extract subsequences converging uniformly on K₁, K₂, … and take the diagonal sequence, which converges uniformly on every compact set. The limit is holomorphic as a locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions.

tasks.entryName: Picard's little theorem
tasks.entryDescription: Original value-distribution/complex-analysis proof; Nevanlinna theory and logarithmic derivative estimates; differential-geometric/Ahlfors–Schwarz approach.
tasks.currentSketch: Assume an entire nonconstant f omits 0 and 1. Then f′/f is entire and has an entire primitive; this gives an entire logarithm g with f=e^g. The omission of 1 forces e^g−1 to have no zeros; standard growth/value-distribution estimates (Picard’s theorem machinery) imply g constant. This sketch suppresses the key estimate.

tasks.entryName: Radon transform injectivity (compactly supported smooth functions)
tasks.entryDescription: Fourier-slice theorem and Fourier inversion; filtered back-projection; moments/polynomial-density arguments. A MathOverflow answer links a lecture-note survey of proofs.
tasks.currentSketch: Take the one-dimensional Fourier transform in the offset variable: the Fourier-slice theorem gives ℱ_t(Rf)(θ,σ)=f̂(σθ). Vanishing Radon data implies f̂ vanishes on every ray, hence everywhere; Fourier inversion gives f=0.

tasks.entryName: Radon transform injectivity (compactly supported smooth functions)
tasks.entryDescription: Fourier-slice theorem and Fourier inversion; filtered back-projection; moments/polynomial-density arguments. A MathOverflow answer links a lecture-note survey of proofs.
tasks.currentSketch: Back-project the line data Rf and apply the ramp filter |ξ| in Fourier space. The Fourier-slice theorem says each projection supplies the restriction of f̂ to a radial line; the ramp-corrected back-projection has Fourier transform a nonzero constant times f̂, so inversion recovers f and injectivity follows.

tasks.routeTitle: moments/polynomial-density arguments. A MathOverflow answer links a lecture-note survey of proofs
tasks.currentSketch: If Rf=0, every directional moment ∫t^m Rf(θ,t)dt equals ∫(x·θ)^m f(x)dx=0. As θ varies, these are all homogeneous moments, so every polynomial pairs to zero with f. Polynomials are dense on a compact set containing supp f; continuity then forces f=0.

tasks.entryName: Fundamental theorem of calculus for line integrals (path independence iff conservative on suitable domains)
tasks.entryDescription: Construct a potential by path integration; differential forms/closed-versus-exact 1-forms on simply connected sets; vector calculus using Green/Stokes.
tasks.routeTitle: Construct a potential by path integration
tasks.currentSketch: Fix x₀ and set φ(x)=∫_{x₀}^x F·dr along any path. Path independence makes φ well-defined; comparing φ(x+h e_i) and φ(x) along a short segment gives ∂ᵢφ=Fᵢ. The reverse implication is the fundamental theorem for line integrals.

tasks.entryName: Fundamental theorem of calculus for line integrals (path independence iff conservative on suitable domains)
tasks.entryDescription: Construct a potential by path integration; differential forms/closed-versus-exact 1-forms on simply connected sets; vector calculus using Green/Stokes.
tasks.routeTitle: differential forms/closed-versus-exact 1-forms on simply connected sets
tasks.currentSketch: The 1-form ω is path-independent on a simply connected domain iff all closed-loop integrals vanish. By Stokes, dω=0 makes integrals invariant under homotopy; simple connectedness contracts loops, so define φ(x)=∫_{x₀}^xω and differentiate to obtain dφ=ω. Conversely exact forms integrate to endpoint differences.

tasks.entryName: Fundamental theorem of calculus for line integrals (path independence iff conservative on suitable domains)
tasks.entryDescription: Construct a potential by path integration; differential forms/closed-versus-exact 1-forms on simply connected sets; vector calculus using Green/Stokes.
tasks.currentSketch: For any two paths from a to b, concatenate one with the reverse of the other to form a loop. Green/Stokes converts its line integral to ∬(curl F)·n; if curl F=0 on a simply connected planar domain, this is zero, proving path independence. Define the potential by integrating along paths.

tasks.entryName: Minkowski inequality for Lᵖ norms
tasks.entryDescription: Hölder duality and integration; convexity/Young's inequality; interpolate from the triangle inequality for simple functions and pass by approximation. State the measure-space and p-range assumptions.
tasks.currentSketch: For 1<p<∞, write ∫|f+g|^p≤∫(|f|+|g|)|f+g|^{p−1}; apply Hölder to each term and divide by ||f+g||_p^{p−1}. This yields ||f+g||_p≤||f||_p+||g||_p; endpoint p=1 is direct, p=∞ follows from sup. Assume measurable functions and finite norms.

tasks.entryName: Riesz–Markov–Kakutani representation theorem (compact Hausdorff version)
tasks.entryDescription: Positive-functional construction by outer measure; Daniell integral approach; duality/measure representation from continuous functions. State the exact real/complex and locally compact variants.
tasks.currentSketch: For positive L:C(K)→R define μ(U)=sup{L(f):0≤f≤1, supp f⊂U}; use partitions of unity to prove finite additivity on disjoint opens and outer regular extension to a Borel measure. Approximation of continuous f by level-set simple functions gives L(f)=∫f dμ; positivity ensures uniqueness.
